newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler launches new compact car with pizazz.
newsitem.headline: Daimler launches new compact car with pizazz.

text.p: Germany's Mercedes-Benz AG, famous for its luxury cars and limos, announced on Tuesday an uncharacteristically glitzy scheme to launch its new A-class compact.
The venerable company plans a touring road show complete with dancers inside in a six-storey high steel cube.

Mercedes said the presentation, which will begin on May 7 in Frankfurt, is a "conscious break away from the well-trodden paths of traditional model introductions" and will highlight a famous Spanish modern theatre and dance group.

The show will mark the market introduction of the new smaller car, expected to be priced from about 30,000 marks ($17,000) -- about half that of other Mercedes vehicles. The car will be available for sale beginning May 5 and in dealer showrooms from October.
"This is going to be a rather unconventional presentation for an unconventional car," said Mercedes executive Jochen Plaecking in announcing plans for the traveling road show.
"We wanted to bring this car to the heart of the cities," he said, noting the break from the usual introduction in which potential customers are invited to local showrooms.

The German carmaker is counting on the novel introduction to lure younger customers to the Mercedes brand and also to help expand the Stuttgart carmaker's sales to one million vehicles by the turn of the century.
Mercedes plans to build up to 200,000 of the units each year at its plant in Rastatt, Germany, and boost its vehicle production from the 1996 level of 645,000 passenger cars.

The focus of activities will be an 18 metre high cube made of steel which will be stationed in the city centre of at least 14 German cities before starting a European tour to Lisbon, Zurich, Prague, Paris and Copenhagen.

The Catalan theatre company La Fura dels Baus ("The Rats from the Sewer"), best known for "terrorising" audiences at a 1989 Sydney performance with chainsaws, shopping trolleys and offal and also opening the Barcelona Summer Olympics, will give a performance in each of the cities.
A group member, Javier Hansel Cereza, told reporters the performance would be based on its "Symbiosis" performance which he said involves a journey into several "microworlds".

Daimler management board member Dieter Zetsche, who is responsible for Mercedes sales and marketing, said the carmaker has about 350,000 potential sales leads in Germany alone and that about 130,000 were tagged as "hot sales leads".

The road show is the latest in Mercedes' efforts to build up a potential customer base for the A-class, which is aimed at 30-something singles, two-person households and hip young families during a generally difficult European sales environment and fierce competition for lower-priced vehicles.
At the Geneva car show, stomping dancers unveiled the car as part of a fevered-pitch routine that included some using the car as a percussion instrument in front of Daimler boss Juergen Schrempp.

Mercedes last year also launched a major advertising campaign with a glitzy brochure with young models reminiscent of a hip fashion catalogue that folds out to 3.6 meters long -- the same length as the car.

The carmaker is venturing into a new segment and will face mass carmakers such as Volkswagen AG and General Motors Corp's Opel and Vauxhall brands. Some industry officials have voiced doubts as to whether the car can succeed.
But Mercedes executives have dismissed criticism about the A-class, saying they have created a new car class with a new presence due in part to the product introduction.
"There is little doubt that it will become a trendsetter and influence car engineering as a whole," Daimler management board member Juergen Hubbert said.
